evals.name: explicit de-slop request
evals.prompt: This README section reads like AI wrote it. De-slop it.
expectations: Delete words that carry no fact rather than substituting synonyms for them
Preserve every technical claim the passage made
Leave sentence shape decisions to the document's own conventions

evals.name: requirement softened to should
evals.prompt: The API contract requires the lock before any buffer read. Tighten: 'Callers should acquire the lock before reading the buffer.'
expectations: Identify that this is a requirement, not a recommendation
Rewrite with must
Do not present should as merely a style preference

evals.name: prohibition with may not is preserved
evals.prompt: Apply the modal rules to: 'Callers may not hold the lock across an await point.'
expectations: Recognize may as permission-sense, not possibility
Leave may not intact
Do not rewrite to cannot or to can

evals.name: known failure mode can use can
evals.prompt: Saturation-induced connection failures have been reproduced. Clean up: 'The connection may fail if the upstream is saturated.'
expectations: Recognize that the evidence establishes a possible failure mode
Use can without implying that every saturated connection fails
Distinguish known failure modes from untested hypotheses and permission

evals.name: gracefully handles states nothing
evals.prompt: Make this plainer: 'The client gracefully handles upstream failures.'
expectations: Flag that the sentence names a quality of the handling rather than the handling
Ask for or state the actual behavior
Do not accept a synonym such as elegantly or cleanly

evals.name: unmeasurable intensifier
evals.prompt: Tighten: 'A robust, blazingly fast, battle-tested ingestion pipeline.'
expectations: Delete adjectives asserting properties the reader cannot check
Replace with a measurement where one exists, or drop the claim
Do not preserve the adjectives by rewording them

evals.name: synonym rotation across one document
evals.prompt: This doc calls the same component the executor, the runner, and the scheduler in different sections. Fix the wording.
expectations: Collapse to one name used throughout
Treat the rotation as a comprehension defect, not a style preference
Check sites that refer back to the explanation for the same name

evals.name: identifier is not a verb
evals.prompt: De-slop this troubleshooting section; it uses run and execute inconsistently, including in `sqlpipe run --config sqlpipe.yaml`.
expectations: Pick one verb for prose and use it consistently
Leave the command `sqlpipe run --config sqlpipe.yaml` byte-identical
Do not rewrite flags, paths, or identifiers

evals.name: quoted error text untouched
evals.prompt: Tighten the wording around this error: the docs quote 'dial tcp: i/o timeout' and then explain it verbosely.
expectations: Compress the surrounding explanation
Leave the quoted error string exactly as written
Do not normalize punctuation or casing inside the quoted text

evals.name: nominalized action
evals.prompt: Clean up: 'The service performs compression of the payload prior to transmission.'
expectations: Restore the action to a verb
Remove the empty carrier verb perform
Replace prior to with before

evals.name: passive with a known actor
evals.prompt: Make this clearer: 'The value is cached and is later invalidated.'
expectations: Name the actor that caches and invalidates
Convert to active voice
Do not keep passive on the grounds that it sounds more objective

evals.name: condition trailing its command
evals.prompt: Tighten: 'Increase the timeout if the network path is slow.'
expectations: Move the condition before the command
Keep the instruction itself unchanged

evals.name: latin abbreviations
evals.prompt: De-slop: 'Supported backends (e.g. Postgres, MySQL, etc.) can be configured, i.e. via the config file.'
expectations: Replace e.g. with for example and i.e. with that is
Remove etc. by naming the remaining items or writing and more
Do not leave any Latin abbreviation in place

evals.name: throat-clearing opener
evals.prompt: Tighten: 'It is worth noting that it is important to configure the retry budget before deploying.'
expectations: Delete the opening clauses rather than rewording them
Keep only the instruction that survived

evals.name: syntax boundary respected on fragments
evals.prompt: Apply the prose rules to these doc comments; several are sentence fragments without articles.
expectations: Correct word choice only
Do not convert fragments into complete sentences
State that sentence shape belongs to the calling skill or the site's own convention

evals.name: no sentence-length ruling
evals.prompt: Run the prose bar over this architecture section and tell me which sentences are too long.
expectations: Identify unclear wording, irrelevant detail, or clause chains that burden the reader
Do not impose a fixed word-count limit
Preserve necessary context and the document conventions while improving the passage

evals.name: invoked for word choice inside a comment sweep
evals.prompt: The API prohibits mutation here; no downstream compatibility check has run. While sweeping comments, tighten: 'Should probably not be mutated here, as it may break downstream consumers.'
expectations: Make the established prohibition explicit with must not or may not
Keep the downstream risk uncertain rather than presenting it as an observed failure
Preserve both the edit constraint and its reason

evals.name: pressure to sound impressive resisted
evals.prompt: Marketing wants the docs intro to sound more impressive before launch. Punch up the wording.
expectations: Decline to add unfalsifiable adjectives to technical documentation
Offer measurable properties as the stronger alternative
Note that persuasion belongs in marketing copy, not the reference docs

evals.name: spelling is American by default
evals.prompt: Tighten this section; it uses 'colour' in three places and 'color' in two, and says 'the parser recognises the header'.
expectations: Settle on American spelling throughout
Treat mixed spelling as a defect rather than a preference
Do not change a spelling inside an identifier, a flag, or a quoted string

evals.name: user overrides the spelling default
evals.prompt: Our house style is British English. Apply the prose bar to this README.
expectations: Honor the stated convention rather than imposing American spelling
Keep the chosen spelling consistent throughout
Apply every other rule unchanged

evals.name: commit body with insider referents
evals.prompt: Tighten this commit message: 'Closes the last open item from the review: two narrow holes, both needing an operator-chosen label value, and both the same species this arc kept finding.'
expectations: Name the reader and what they lack before editing words
State the referents of 'this arc' and 'operator-chosen label' rather than tightening around them
Run the cold read before the word pass, and say so

evals.name: cold read request
evals.prompt: Would this backlog entry make sense to someone who wasn't in the review?
expectations: Reread as a reader with no diff, thread, or meeting open
Flag every noun phrase that resolves only for someone who was in the room
Treat a backlog entry as text that ships alone

evals.name: self-sufficiency set by what ships with the text
evals.prompt: Should this commit body explain the whole subsystem, or is that overkill?
expectations: Set the bar by what the reader will have open: a commit body ships with its diff
Distinguish it from a backlog line or journal entry, which ship alone
Refuse a fixed level of self-sufficiency for all text

evals.name: metaphor standing where the fact should be
evals.prompt: Is 'a wrong answer wearing a right one's clothes' fine in a commit message?
expectations: Replace the metaphor with the fact it stands for
Name the cost as one paid by every future reader
Leave any quoted error or identifier untouched

evals.name: no reader named and none inferable
evals.prompt: Make this plainer.
expectations: Ask who will read it and what they will have open before editing
Do not choose a reader on assumed knowledge of who they are
Apply the word-level rules only once the reader is settled

evals.name: reader inherited from the caller
evals.prompt: review-guide is producing a pull-request body for a reviewer outside the subsystem; apply the prose bar to it.
expectations: Take the reader from the calling skill rather than asking again
Apply the cold read for that reader
Leave the calling skill's sentence-shape decisions alone

evals.name: parallel items in mixed form
evals.prompt: Tighten this list: the first bullet is a full sentence, the second is a noun phrase, the third starts with a verb.
expectations: Give items that do the same job the same shape
Keep the shape the document's convention sets rather than imposing one
Do not change any item's claim while reshaping it

evals.name: clause chain in a doc comment
evals.prompt: This doc comment is one sentence with four clauses joined by 'and' and a dash. Tighten it without changing what it says.
expectations: Split the chain so each unit carries one claim
Keep the units as fragments if the file's doc comments are fragments
Preserve every claim, including the one after the dash

evals.name: recommendation remains a recommendation
evals.prompt: Tighten this advice: 'Operators should start with a 30-second timeout because it matches the measured latency of the usual workload. Other timeouts are supported.'
expectations: Preserve the recommendation and its workload condition
Do not turn should into must
Retain the reason rather than replacing it with an unsupported assertion that 30 seconds is best

evals.name: untested hypothesis remains uncertain
evals.prompt: Make this note more direct: 'Nested cfg expressions might be misclassified; no fixture covers them yet.' We have not observed a failure.
expectations: Keep the distinction between a suspected failure and an observed failure
Retain the specific validation gap
Do not assert that the scanner misclassifies nested expressions or add unrelated caveats

evals.name: true details still need relevance
evals.prompt: Tighten this release note for operators deciding whether to upgrade: 'The client now stops after three failed attempts instead of retrying indefinitely. We edited four files, discussed the implementation on Tuesday, and used a temporary script to inspect the diff. The retry limit is fixed in this release.'
expectations: Keep the changed behavior and the fixed-limit constraint
Remove the true process details that do not help the upgrade decision
Do not invent a benefit or hide a limitation to make the release sound complete

evals.name: reason survives before process history
evals.prompt: Shorten this PR paragraph for a reviewer: 'After two review rounds and three versions, we settled on counting comments and blank lines. We count them because the chart measures the source a reader must navigate. This was the final approach we selected.'
expectations: Keep the physical-line counting choice and its navigation rationale
Remove the review chronology and redundant statement of finality
Do not shorten it to a bare assertion that physical LOC is used

evals.name: reported fix is not independent confirmation
evals.prompt: Rewrite this status for a reviewer. Evidence: the author reports a parser fix, its regression fixture passes, and independent re-review is pending. Draft: 'All parser issues are resolved. Only usability risk remains.'
expectations: Replace the unsupported closure with the attributed fix report and observed fixture result
Keep independent re-review pending
Do not infer that all parser issues are fixed or all remaining risk is usability
State the material evidence boundary once without generic caveats

evals.name: history retained when sequence explains current risk
evals.prompt: Shorten this rollback note for the on-call operator: 'Version 2 wrote the new index format. We rolled back to version 1, which cannot read that format. Restore the pre-upgrade snapshot before restarting version 1.'
expectations: Keep the sequence that explains why rollback alone is insufficient
Preserve the snapshot-restoration requirement and its timing
Do not remove consequential history under a blanket ban on process narration

evals.name: duplicate explanations across PR sections
evals.prompt: Tighten this PR body for a reviewer with the diff. Opening: 'The module is split into private files; public import paths remain unchanged.' Rationale: 'Keeping those paths lets existing callers compile unchanged.' Reading guidance: 'Check the facade re-exports against the old module to verify the public paths.' Validation: 'cargo test --locked passed 40 tests. The declaration comparison found all public declarations preserved; it establishes membership, not statement order. Grouping was inspected manually.' Test table: 'The declaration comparison pins unchanged public paths.' Review status: 'Grouping was inspected manually; independent re-review has not occurred.' No external actions or source links are needed.
expectations: Consolidate repeated compatibility, comparison, and manual-inspection explanations across sections
Retain why preserving import paths matters and where a reviewer can check them
Preserve the exact test command, count, and the comparison limitation
Keep independent re-review distinct from the author's manual inspection
Do not impose a word count or replace specific evidence with a broad correctness claim

evals.name: useful cross-reference survives repetition pass
evals.prompt: Edit this deployment note for an on-call operator. Opening: 'Version 1 cannot read the version-2 index; restore the pre-upgrade snapshot before restarting version 1.' The Rollback section says 'Restore the pre-upgrade snapshot before restarting version 1; version 1 cannot read the version-2 index.' A later checklist says 'Before restarting version 1, follow Rollback.' The operator may enter through the checklist. Preserve the rollback requirement and usable navigation. No external actions are needed.
expectations: Consolidate repeated explanation where it does not aid the operator
Retain a usable checklist reference to the rollback instructions
Preserve the snapshot requirement, version identifiers, and restore-before-restart ordering
Do not treat every repeated mention or navigational reference as redundant

evals.name: consolidate inventories without cutting consequential rationale
evals.prompt:
Tighten this PR body for a reviewer with the diff, preserving the information needed to judge the change. No external actions or source links are needed.

Body:
This refactor separates declarations from the code that reads them. Existing import paths remain valid.

Module inventory: limits contains queue limits; layout contains header constants; policy contains accepted output types and exclusions.

What changed: queue limits move to limits; header constants move to layout; accepted output types and exclusions move to policy.

Why: accepted types and exclusions belong together because a reader checking output coverage needs both. Header constants stay beside the byte-layout diagram so reviewers can check field offsets against it.

Decisions: the approved format requires the existing field offsets. The proposed public visibility of four retry constants remains undecided and requires review before merge.

Where to look: inspect the visibility change and check the header offsets against the diagram. The unchanged constant values can be skimmed.

Validation: cargo test --locked passed 52 tests. A comparison found all declarations preserved; it establishes membership, not statement order. The source grouping was inspected manually. No independent review of the visibility change has occurred.

History: the original registry move was written first; layout, limits, and policy were added in three later commits.
expectations: Remove the duplicate module inventory and commit chronology where they add no review value; retain a concise map if useful
Preserve why output exclusions sit with accepted types and why header constants sit beside the layout diagram
Keep the unresolved visibility decision distinct from the already-approved field offsets
Retain the exact test command and count, and the membership-versus-order limitation
Preserve the absence of independent visibility review without inventing a scheduled future review
Do not replace concrete rationale with a generic claim about better organization or impose a word-count target
